The diagram shows the production possibility curves of two countries, X and Y. country X capital 50 goods 40 country Y 0 20 60 100 consumer goods What can be concluded from the diagram?

options.A: Both countries have decreasing opportunity cost in the production of consumer goods.
options.B: Both countries should produce 40 units of capital goods and 20 units of consumer goods.
options.C: Country Y has constant opportunity cost in the production of consumer goods.
options.D: Country Y is producing more consumer goods than country X.

questions.questionText: In 2020, there was a worldwide pandemic. High-income countries quickly developed a vaccine. Low-income countries built high-tech factories to manufacture large quantities of the vaccine for export. What explains this international division of labour? high-income countries low-income countries

options.A: availability of specialists in lower costs of production research and development
options.B: scarce human resources over-supply of unskilled labour
options.C: many people tended to many people tended to avoid the disease catch the disease
options.D: no government control strict government control over resource allocation over resource allocation

questions.questionText: How can a public good become a private good?

options.A: Consumers are dissatisfied with the performance of state-run services.
options.B: New technological developments make the good excludable.
options.C: The government privatises the industry producing the good.
options.D: The price of the good increases so it becomes more profitable.

options.A: to act as a signal to firms when allocating resources
options.B: to maximise consumer surplus
options.C: to provide an incentive to firms to produce goods
options.D: to ration scarce resources

options.B: A positive price change encourages a positive output change along the supply curve.
options.C: Fresh vegetables has a horizontal supply curve.
options.D: There is a seasonal time lag involved in planting and harvesting more fresh vegetables.

What is an example of a transfer payment?

options.A: a household moving savings from one bank account to another
options.B: a monthly repayment on a loan used to buy a new cooker
options.C: the amount paid to transport goods from one city to another
options.D: grants paid to students by the government

questions.questionText: Which statement correctly describes an increase in real GDP?

options.A: Nominal GDP rising faster than nominal income.
options.B: Nominal GDP rising faster than the rate of inflation.
options.C: The rate of inflation rising faster than aggregate demand.
options.D: The rate of inflation rising faster than nominal income.

questions.questionText: An open economy with a government sector is in equilibrium. Households in this economy save $100 million and firms spend $150 million on investment. Which combination of the budget balance and the current account balance would lead to an equilibrium position on the circular flow of income? budget balance current account balance

options.A: $100m deficit $50m deficit
options.B: $100m deficit $50m surplus
options.C: $100m surplus $50m deficit
options.D: $100m surplus $50m surplus

questions.questionText: An economy’s manufacturing share of real GDP fell from 30% in 1990 to 12% in 2023. Which type of unemployment would have resulted from this?

options.A: cyclical
options.B: frictional
options.C: structural
options.D: voluntary

questions.questionText: Which statement is not correct?

options.A: The long-run aggregate supply curve can be downward sloping.
options.B: The long-run aggregate supply curve can be horizontal.
options.C: The long-run aggregate supply curve can be upward sloping.
options.D: The long-run aggregate supply curve can be vertical.

questions.questionText: A government decides to raise most of its revenues from indirect taxes. What would increase the effectiveness of this policy?

options.A: an increasing trend towards bartering of goods
options.B: increasing interest rates on household savings
options.C: increasing occurrence of informal markets in the economy
options.D: placing taxes on goods and services which have a price-inelastic demand

options.A: a reduction in government spending on training
options.B: an increase in support for technological improvement
options.C: a reduction in payments to the unemployed
options.D: an increase in privatisation of industry
